newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul to allow investment firms to raise capital.
newsitem.headline: Seoul to allow investment firms to raise capital.

text.p: South Korea's Ministry of Finance and Economy said on Monday it would allow three Seoul-based investment firms to raise capital in a bid to boost the sagging stock market.
The ministry said in a statement it expected the capital increases to be used as funds to buy more shares.

The ministry said the three investment firms -- Korea Investment Trust Co, Daehan Investment Trust Co and Citizens Investment Trust Management Co -- would be allowed to increase their capital by a combined 260 billion won.

The ministry also said it would soon approve plans by Samsung Securities Co and Ssangyong Investment and Securities Co to set up trust management joint ventures with foreign companies. No time table was given.
Samsung plans to form a joint venture with a JP Morgan and Co unit and Ssangyong with Franklin/Templeton Group, the ministry statement said.
Fund receipts by the two joint ventures are expected to amount to between one trillion and 1.5 trillion won in initial stages after establishment, the ministry statement said.

The nation's 14 major trust management firms will also be encouraged to develop and sell new products that can better accommodate diverse customer demands for investment instruments, the statement said.
The Seoul stock market has been languishing due to fears of oversupply of shares amid a low level of fund influx into the market, market analysts said.
The composite stock index closed Monday at this year's lowest level of 716.45, down 14.99 points, or 2.05 percent, on the day.
This was a fall of 27.4 percent from this year's highest level of 986.84 set on May 7.
Brokers said the government's plan to sell about 360 billion won worth of shares in state-run Korea Telecom on November 28 and 29 further dampened market sentiment.
